orientation.text: Identifies the language family, version, compiler or runtime, and relevant framework assumptions.
Uses repository evidence to identify build, package, formatter, linter, type-check, and test commands.
Reads repository rules and maintained code in the affected subsystem before choosing a shape.
Models current behavior, callers, consumers, data, state, errors, and compatibility obligations.
Makes invariants, concurrency, cancellation, resource ownership, lifecycle, and recovery explicit.

design_judgment.text: Chooses the layer that owns the behavior or shared invariant.
Compares only a few credible options when a real tradeoff exists, including keeping the current shape when viable.
Selects the design using project evidence, compatibility, operability, debuggability, and verification cost.
Preserves or deliberately changes public, data, runtime, and migration compatibility within authorization.

implementation_quality.text: Uses language- and ecosystem-native types, naming, interfaces, and error handling.
Makes ownership, cleanup, transactions, and resource lifetime explicit and correct.
Handles concurrency, cancellation, timeouts, ordering, and shutdown according to project idioms.
Keeps external boundaries, validation, state transitions, dependencies, and compatibility semantics explicit.
Preserves useful error context and makes failure and recovery diagnosable.

maintainability_audit.text: Keeps names, control flow, and decomposition understandable to maintainers.
Justifies every new field, state, branch, helper, layer, dependency, file, and test by a current consumer or requirement.
Rejects boilerplate symmetry, duplicated logic, pass-through layering, and generalized helpers without evidence.
Preserves local asymmetry when domain behavior, compatibility, or subsystem evidence justifies it.
Leaves behavior, ownership, failure context, and recovery paths observable and diagnosable.

verification.text: Prioritizes project-native behavior or public-contract tests over incidental implementation details.
Tests relevant failure, recovery, cancellation, timeout, duplicate, ordering, resource, or compatibility behavior.
Checks adjacent consumers and shared contracts when the change crosses a semantic seam.
Fixes failures attributable to the change and reruns the relevant verification loop.
Reports exact checks, blockers, assumptions, unproven behavior, and residual risk without overclaiming.

forbidden_patterns.text: Does not add abstraction, configuration, dependency, state, or performance work for hypothetical future needs.
Does not add mechanically mirrored or pass-through wrappers without a real boundary or behavior.
Does not swallow errors, use catch-all handling, or silently discard failure context.
Does not use assertions, casts, non-null, warning, or type suppression to hide a modeling defect.
Does not add production branches or hooks that exist only to satisfy tests.
Does not claim or make performance improvements without relevant baseline or measurement evidence.
Does not claim or imply human authorship; it evaluates observable engineering properties instead.
